explainer.pickup_anywhere: When enabled, patrons can collect a request at any eligible pickup location in the consortium, not only at their own library. Note that individual pickup locations must also be enabled for pickup anywhere separately.
explainer.re_resolution: When enabled, re-resolution will be active for this consortium. This means that if the chosen supplier cannot fulfil a request, OpenRS DCB automatically looks for another supplier instead of failing the request.
explainer.own_library_borrowing: When enabled, items held by the patron's own library are included when OpenRS DCB resolves a request.
explainer.trigger_supplier_renewal: When enabled, if a loan is renewed at the borrowing library, OpenRS DCB mirrors that renewal at the supplying library.
explainer.virtual_patron_names_visible: When enabled, virtual patron records will carry the real patron's name. Leave off to keep virtual patrons anonymous.
explainer.deny_library_mapping_edit: When enabled, this prevents library staff from editing their mappings in DCB Admin for Libraries. Leave disabled if you want to manage mappings centrally.
explainer.select_unavailable: Items that are currently on loan or otherwise unavailable are still offered when DCB resolves a request, rather than skipped.

config_fields.json_mode_warning: Advanced mode. Everything the guided form asks for still has to be present, and switching back will drop any keys the guided form does not know about.
config_fields.unmapped_keys: These keys were in the JSON and have no guided field, so they will not be saved: {{keys}}
config_fields.base_url_qualifier_description: Distinguishes two systems that share a base URL, such as two Alma institutions on one regional gateway. Without it DCB treats them as one system. Use the institution code.
config_fields.virtual_patron_branch_id_description: The branch virtual patrons are registered at, which must be one where the DCB patron codes are defined. Leave blank to use the ILL location.
config_fields.borrower_lending_flow_description: Leave blank for the standard flow, where DCB creates a virtual bib and item. ILL places the hold through Polaris' ILL request workflow instead.
config_fields.hold_fetching_delay_description: Seconds to wait before reading back a hold DCB has just placed.
config_fields.hold_fetching_max_retry_description: How many times to try reading back a hold before giving up.
config_fields.harvest_watermark_overlap_minutes_descri: Minutes each harvest re-reads before the last one, to catch records changed while it ran. Every minute is re-harvested on every cycle, so keep it small.
config_fields.enable_double_delete_description: Delete the virtual bib and item DCB created when a request ends, rather than marking them deleted.
config_fields.no_renew_collection_code_description: The collection code DCB sets on an item to stop it being renewed. Koha's ItemsDeniedRenewal preference must name it.
config_fields.virtual_patron_category_description: The Koha patron category a visiting patron is created in until patron types are mapped. Koha refuses the patron unless this category exists.
config_fields.sierra_api_version_description: Choose an older version only for a Sierra that does not serve v6. DCB is tested against v6.
config_fields.virtual_patron_email_description: The address this system sends visiting patrons' hold and pickup notices to. Use a mailbox the consortium reads, never a patron's own address: every visiting patron shares it.
config_fields.do_not_renew_note_description: The internal note added to an item DCB has stopped being renewed, so this library's staff know why. Write it in the language they work in.
config_fields.recommended_missing_body: The Host LMS will be created without these, but requests are likely to fail later: {{fields}}
config_fields.ingest_description: Whether DCB harvests bibliographic records from this system.
config_fields.default_agency_code_description: The agency to attribute a patron to when their home location has no mapping. Leave blank on a shared system: with several libraries here, no single agency can stand in.
config_fields.ors_default_agency_code_description: The agency DCB names for this appliance in NCIP messages. Required whether or not the appliance serves several libraries.
config_fields.shared_system_description: Set this when more than one participating library is hosted on this system. DCB then requires every branch to be mapped to an agency explicitly, instead of falling back to a default agency or a wildcard, either of which would silently attribute one library's patrons or holdings to another.
config_fields.shared_system_conflict: A shared system cannot have a default agency code. With several libraries on one system, no single agency can stand in for an unmapped location - map each library's locations to its agency instead.
config_fields.page_size_description: How many records DCB requests per harvest page. 100 is a reasonable starting point.
config_fields.alma_url_description: The regional Ex Libris API gateway your Alma instance is served from, e.g. https://api-na.hosted.exlibrisgroup.com. Your region is listed under “Calling Alma APIs”.
config_fields.alma_base_url_description: Your institution's own Alma domain, with no path, e.g. https://example.alma.exlibrisgroup.com. This is the host DCB harvests records from, not the API gateway.
config_fields.alma_apikey_description: An Alma API key with read and write access to Users and Bibs, and read-only access to Configuration. Holdings, items and requests are part of Bibs and Users.
config_fields.alma_api_docs_link: See the Ex Libris Alma API documentation.
config_fields.alma_item_docs_link: See the Ex Libris item schema documentation.
config_fields.alma_connection_group_description: If your Alma system restricts access by IP address, the OpenRS DCB server's IP must be whitelisted before these details will work. Ask your OpenRS team or hosting provider for the address.
config_fields.alma_resource_sharing_group_description: The Alma libraries, locations and codes DCB moves items through. They must exist in Alma first. Never use your Resource Sharing Library (RES_SHARE by default, with its IN_RS_REQ and OUT_RS_REQ locations) for any of them: Alma refuses holds placed there with error 401129.
config_fields.alma_harvesting_group_description: DCB harvests bib records from Alma over OAI-PMH, which the Alma lending workflow depends on. If only your OAI services are IP restricted, the DCB server's IP still has to be whitelisted for them.
config_fields.alma_institution_code_description: Your Alma OAI-PMH institution code, e.g. 01ABC_DEF. DCB builds the harvest address from it, so a wrong value stops ingest rather than the API.
config_fields.alma_sharing_library_code_description: The code of the Alma library every lending hold is placed for pickup at. Scanning an item in anywhere else puts it in transit, which is how DCB knows it is on its way. It must hold none of the items you lend.
config_fields.alma_sharing_circ_desk_code_description: A circulation desk with a hold shelf in the sharing library. When set, lending holds go to this desk rather than to the library.
config_fields.alma_alternative_sharing_library_code_de: Where holds go for items the sharing library owns itself, when no sharing desk is set. It must be a different library from the sharing library.
config_fields.alma_request_cancellation_reason_descrip: A code from your RequestCancellationReasons code table, sent whenever DCB cancels a request. It is what your staff see in the request's history.
config_fields.alma_virtual_item_library_code_descripti: The code of the Alma library DCB creates virtual items at. Alma cannot report a patron's home location reliably, so this has to be agreed with your Alma staff.
config_fields.alma_virtual_item_location_code_descript: The code of the location within that library where virtual items are created. It must exist: DCB reads it from Alma each time it creates a virtual item.
config_fields.alma_default_circ_desk_code_description: The code of the circulation desk OpenRS DCB scans items in at. It must exist in each library DCB acts in.
config_fields.alma_pickup_circ_desk_description: The code of the circulation desk OpenRS DCB checks items out at, to a visiting patron or to one of your patrons collecting at another member. Alma refuses a checkout at a desk that cannot loan items from the item's library.
config_fields.alma_item_policy_description: The Alma item policy applied to the virtual items DCB creates. Codes come from the ItemPolicy code table.
config_fields.alma_user_identifier_description: The Alma user identifier type DCB tags visiting patrons' accounts with. Leave blank to use INST_ID.
config_fields.alma_no_renew_item_policy_description: The item policy DCB sets on an item to stop it being renewed. Alma needs a loan rule that refuses renewal for this policy. Leave blank to use DCB_NO_RENEW.
config_fields.alma_virtual_patron_barcode_prefix_descr: A prefix on the barcodes of the accounts DCB creates for visiting patrons. Leave blank unless your barcodes collide with another member's.
config_fields.alma_oai_set_description: The OAI set you are making available to OpenRS DCB. Leave blank to harvest everything your institution publishes.
config_fields.alma_metadata_prefix_description: The OAI-PMH metadata prefix DCB harvests with. Alma publishes marc21. Harvesting cannot start without this.
config_fields.sierra_base_url_description: The root URL of the Sierra system, without the API path.
config_fields.sierra_key_description: The client key for the Sierra API account.
config_fields.sierra_secret_description: The client secret paired with the API key.
config_fields.patron_search_tag_description: The Sierra varfield tag DCB searches patrons by.
config_fields.virtual_patron_pin_description: PIN applied to the virtual patron records DCB creates.
config_fields.get_holds_retry_attempts_description: How many times to retry reading a patron's holds before giving up.
config_fields.place_hold_delay_description: Seconds to wait before placing a hold, for systems that need settling time.
config_fields.get_hold_delay_description: Seconds to wait before reading a hold back after placing it.
config_fields.virtual_item_library_code_description: The library virtual items are created at.
config_fields.virtual_item_location_code_description: The location virtual items are created at.
config_fields.folio_base_url_description: The base URL for this FOLIO tenant.
config_fields.folio_apikey_description: An edge API key for the FOLIO tenant, issued by your FOLIO administrator.
config_fields.metadata_prefix_description: OAI-PMH metadata prefix used for harvesting.
config_fields.folio_record_syntax_description: Sent as recordSyntax on every harvest request. Leave blank to use oai_dc, which every FOLIO on production uses; set it only for a FOLIO whose edge-oai-pmh expects something else.
config_fields.folio_metadata_prefix_description: The OAI-PMH metadata format DCB harvests. Leave blank to use marc21_withholdings, MARC with holdings.
config_fields.polaris_base_url_description: The root URL of the Polaris system.
config_fields.base_url_application_services_descriptio: Base URL of the Polaris Application Services API.
config_fields.domain_id_description: The Polaris domain the staff account belongs to.
config_fields.logon_branch_id_description: Branch the DCB staff account signs in against.
config_fields.logon_user_id_description: Polaris user ID of the DCB staff account.
config_fields.staff_username_description: Username of the DCB staff account.
config_fields.staff_password_description: Password of the DCB staff account.
config_fields.papi_description: Polaris PAPI connection details. DCB requires this section to be present.
config_fields.services_description: Polaris application services details. DCB requires this section to be present.
config_fields.services_organisation_id_description: Organisation identifier used by application services.
config_fields.services_site_domain_description: Site domain the staff account authenticates against.
config_fields.services_patron_barcode_prefix_descripti: Prefix applied to virtual patron barcodes.
config_fields.item_description: Defaults applied to the virtual items DCB creates. DCB requires this section to be present.
config_fields.barcode_prefix_description: Prefix applied to virtual item barcodes.
config_fields.ill_location_id_description: Location identifier used for interlibrary loan items.
config_fields.fine_code_id_description: Fine code applied to virtual items.

config_fields.renewal_limit_av_description: Renewal limit applied to audiovisual virtual items, where it differs from the standard one.

request_volume.what: How many requests entered DCB in each period of the window.
request_volume.how: Transitions into SUBMITTED_TO_DCB per bucket, from the audit trail. The bucket is a day, a week or a month depending on the length of the window.
request_volume.not: It counts requests that ARRIVED, not requests that were filled. A period can be busy and unsuccessful. The most recent bucket is left out of the line entirely until it closes, because a partial period always looks like a fall.

trend_direction.what: Whether a measure is moving, and whether the movement is the good one.
trend_direction.how: The mean of the most recent third of buckets against the mean of the third before it. A change smaller than the noise floor - one percentage point for a rate, five per cent for a count - is reported as no clear change rather than as a direction. Fewer than nine closed buckets is reported as too short a window.
trend_direction.not: It is not a forecast and not a significance test. It says the recent period differs from the one before it, nothing about why, and a single extraordinary week inside the recent third will move it.

turnaround_trend.what: Whether the wait between a request arriving and the item being loaned is getting longer.
turnaround_trend.how: The median and 95th percentile of that duration, per bucket, for the requests that REACHED the loan in that bucket.
turnaround_trend.not: A bucket holds the requests that finished in it, not the ones that started in it, so a spell of very slow requests appears when they complete rather than when they arrived. A bucket with no completions is absent from the line rather than drawn as zero.

supplier_response_trend.what: Whether suppliers are taking longer to confirm the requests placed with them.
supplier_response_trend.how: Placed at the supplier to confirmed by it, as a median and a 95th percentile per bucket, scoped on the supplying library.
supplier_response_trend.not: It measures the supplier, not DCB: the time DCB spent choosing that supplier is deliberately outside it. Requests never confirmed are not in the figure, so a supplier that ignores everything can look fast.

transit_dwell_trend.what: Whether items are spending longer in transit between libraries.
transit_dwell_trend.how: Median and 95th percentile dwell in the chosen transit status, per bucket, for the items that left it in that bucket.
transit_dwell_trend.not: It measures the status, not the courier: an item scanned late at the receiving end is indistinguishable from one that travelled slowly. A system that does not report the return leg contributes nothing to it rather than contributing a zero.

method.title: How {{label}} is calculated
method.sample_low: Only {{count}} observations in this window - a single outlier moves this figure.
method.sample_unknown: This endpoint reports percentiles without a count, so how many requests are behind this figure is not known here.

requests_fulfilled.what: Requests that reached a settled outcome in the window, whether they were filled or not.
requests_fulfilled.how: The successful and failed counts from the borrower fulfilment query, added together. Successful means the request reached loaned, completed or finalised.
requests_fulfilled.not: Requests still in flight when the window closed are in neither count, so a busy week looks smaller until its requests settle.

fill_rate.what: The share of settled requests that reached the patron.
fill_rate.how: Successful divided by successful plus failed, over the same window. The delta compares it with the equal-length window immediately before.
fill_rate.not: It says nothing about how long the fill took, and nothing about requests still open. A service that fills everything slowly scores the same as one that fills everything quickly.

error_rate.what: The share of settled requests that did not reach the patron.
error_rate.how: The exact complement of the fill rate: one minus successful over successful plus failed.
error_rate.not: It does not separate a cancellation from a breakdown. The failure taxonomy panel answers why; this only answers how often.

libraries_active.what: Members that borrowed or supplied at least once in the window.
libraries_active.how: One row per Host LMS from the net flow query, counting those whose borrowed and supplied counts do not both sit at zero.
libraries_active.not: It counts Host LMS systems, not libraries. Where several libraries share one system they cannot be told apart here, so a shared system counts once however many members sit behind it.

net_flow.what: Whether this library gave the network more than it took.
net_flow.how: Items supplied to other members minus items borrowed from them, over the window. Errored requests are excluded from both sides.
net_flow.not: It is a count of requests, not of value or of effort, and it says nothing about which titles moved.

items_supplied.what: Requests this library filled for another member's patron.
items_supplied.how: Requests whose supplying Host LMS is this library, excluding errored ones.
items_supplied.not: Local fulfilment is excluded: an item this library supplied to its own patron is not network traffic.

turnaround_to_loan.what: How long a patron waits between asking for an item and being issued it.
turnaround_to_loan.how: Median and 95th percentile of the interval from request creation to the first audit entry reaching loaned. A status re-entered during tracking counts once.
turnaround_to_loan.not: Requests that never reached loaned are absent, and so are those still open. A rising median can therefore mean faster failures as well as slower loans.

turnaround_to_finalise.what: The full administrative cycle, from request to the point where nothing is left to do.
turnaround_to_finalise.how: Median and 95th percentile from request creation to the first audit entry reaching finalised.
turnaround_to_finalise.not: Finalisation trails the patron's experience by a long way - the item has usually been back on the shelf for some time - so this is an operations figure, not a service one.

supplier_response.what: How quickly a supplying library answers a request placed with it.
supplier_response.how: Median from the request being placed at the supplying agency to that supplier confirming it, using the earliest audit entry for each so a tracking repeat cannot double-count.
supplier_response.not: It deliberately does not start at request creation, which would fold DCB's own resolution time into a supplier's score. Across several libraries it is one figure per supplier, so no single number is shown.

transit_dwell.what: How long an item spends in transit on one leg of its journey.
transit_dwell.how: Median time between the request entering the transit status and leaving it, taken from the audit trail.
transit_dwell.not: It depends on the host LMS reporting the status at all. A system that never sets it produces no observation, which is shown as not reported rather than as a fast leg. A journey that began before the window opened is excluded.

failure_taxonomy.what: Why requests failed, grouped by the reason rather than counted together.
failure_taxonomy.how: Requests that ended in error or cancellation, or whose previous status was that no item was selectable at any agency, bucketed by that reason.
failure_taxonomy.not: A request that failed and was then re-resolved successfully is not here: it succeeded. The rescued count in the header is where those appear.

supplier_reliability.what: How often each supplying library delivered what it was asked for.
supplier_reliability.how: Per supplier, requests that reached loaned, completed or finalised against those that errored, were cancelled, or found no selectable item.
supplier_reliability.not: A supplier that is asked rarely can look perfect or terrible on a handful of requests, so read it with the count beside it.

trading_partners.what: Which members this library exchanges most traffic with, in each direction.
trading_partners.how: Requests grouped by the partner at the other end, excluding errored requests and local fulfilment, because a failed request is not traffic and a local loan is not a partnership.
trading_partners.not: A partner is never one of the caller's own libraries. Consortium-wide there is no own set to exclude, so the lists rank every supplier and every borrower.

unfillable_demand.what: Titles patrons asked for that nothing in the network could satisfy.
unfillable_demand.how: Requests whose previous status was that no item was selectable at any agency, grouped by title.
unfillable_demand.not: It is demand nobody could meet, not demand that failed for another reason - a request that errored during transit is in the failure taxonomy instead.

peer_benchmarks.what: This library's volume and outcomes beside every other member's.
peer_benchmarks.how: One row per borrowing library, with its request count, checkouts, successes and failures over the window.
peer_benchmarks.not: It is deliberately not pseudonymised: members are named, because a benchmark nobody can act on is decoration.

checkout_rate.what: How often an item that arrived was actually collected.
checkout_rate.how: Requests that reached loaned as a share of those that got far enough to be collectable.
checkout_rate.not: An item a patron never came for is a cost the fill rate cannot see, which is why this sits beside it rather than inside it.

cost_avoidance.what: What these fulfilments would have cost through traditional interlibrary loan.
cost_avoidance.how: Successful fulfilments in the window multiplied by a unit cost you supply. No cost is shipped with the product.
cost_avoidance.not: It is an assumption multiplied by a count, not a measurement. The count is ours; the unit cost is yours, and the figure is only as defensible as that number.

welcome.context: You are using $t(app.name) to manage the $t(app.dcb_full) configuration for the {{consortium_name}} consortium.

intro.title: Before you start
intro.time: This takes about ten minutes. You can leave at any point and pick up where you stopped - nothing you have saved is lost.
intro.needs_consortium: Your consortium's name, the date it launched, and its website.
intro.needs_contact: An email address for whoever should be contacted about the consortium as a whole.
intro.needs_hostlms: For the last step, your first library's Host LMS connection details: its base URL and API credentials. If you do not have those to hand, add your libraries later - everything before it still saves.

setup.needs_consortium: This step needs your consortium to exist first. Go back and tell us about your consortium, and this will open up.

error.title: We could not check how far along your setup is
error.message: This is a problem reading from DCB, not a problem with your consortium. Reload to try again.

appearance.label: Appearance
appearance.title: First, how should DCB Admin look to you?
appearance.subtitle: Tell us what you want your DCB Admin experience to look like. You can change any of it later, and it only affects your own account.

consortium.label: Your consortium
consortium.title: Tell us about your consortium
consortium.subtitle: This is the organisation everything else belongs to: its name, when it launched, and where people can find it.

howItWorks.label: How requesting works
howItWorks.title: How should requesting work?
howItWorks.subtitle: These decide what your patrons and staff can do. Pick what suits your consortium - none of it is permanent.

contacts.label: Contacts
contacts.title: Who should we contact?
contacts.subtitle: The person to reach about the consortium as a whole. You can add more people afterwards.

discovery.label: Discovery branding
discovery.title: How should discovery look to your patrons?
discovery.subtitle: Discovery is what your patrons search. This is the name, the marks and the welcome they see when they arrive.

libraries.label: Your libraries
libraries.title: Now let's add your libraries
libraries.subtitle: Add one at a time with the guided wizard, or upload a spreadsheet if you already have your members listed.

appearance.scope_note: These are your own preferences. They do not change what anyone else sees, and they do not change how discovery looks to patrons.

consortium.already_title: Your consortium is already set up
consortium.already_body: {{name}} already exists on this system, so there is nothing to create here. You can edit its details on the Consortium page at any time.

discovery.preview_caveat: An approximation of the arrangement: if your discovery system is using the OpenRS-provided branding, this is what it could look like. This will vary between systems.

libraries.already_body_one: There is 1 library on this system.
libraries.already_body_other: There are {{count}} libraries on this system.
libraries.one_body: The guided wizard: the library, its Host LMS and connection details, its mappings and its pickup locations. Best for your first library, and for any library you are setting up carefully.
libraries.many_body: Create many libraries at once from a CSV or TSV file. You will see exactly what would change before anything is written.
libraries.after_import: Adding a library creates the record. Its mappings, pickup locations and ingest are set up per library afterwards - the Onboarding page tracks what each one still needs.

banner.title: Your setup is not finished
banner.fresh_body: Nothing has been set up on this system yet. It takes about ten minutes, and you can stop and come back at any point.

done.title: You are set up
done.subtitle_one: Your consortium exists and has 1 library.
done.subtitle_other: Your consortium exists and has {{count}} libraries.
done.revisit_hint: Anything here can be changed - open any step to go back to it.
done.outstanding: You passed over: {{steps}}. Each one is still there when you want it.
done.next_steps: Adding a library is the start of configuring it. The Onboarding page shows what each library still needs - its mappings, its pickup locations, and whether its records have been ingested.

import.title: Import libraries from a spreadsheet
import.explanation: Upload a CSV or TSV file with one row per library. Nothing is created until you have seen what would change and confirmed it.
import.limits: Up to {{rows}} rows and {{size}}. CSV or TSV; the separator is detected from the file.
import.too_large: That file is {{size}}, which is over the {{max}} limit. Split it into smaller files, or check that it is a spreadsheet export and not a whole workbook.
import.no_rows: That file has a header but no library rows in it.
import.unknown_headers: Columns we do not recognise, and have ignored: {{headers}}. Everything else in the file has been read normally.
import.summary: {{create}} to create, {{update}} already exist, {{reject}} cannot be used.
import.table_caption: Every row in your file, and what would happen to it. Rows matching a library that already exists are not ticked - tick one only if you mean to overwrite it.
import.will_update: A library with this agency code already exists. Tick to overwrite it.

service_capabilities.subtitle: DCB Admin runs against more than one dcb-service release. These features are switched on per environment once its dcb-service is new enough. This deployment reports version {{version}}.

feature.host_lms_probes: Host LMS checks, the last connection check and ingest counts for chosen libraries

settings_inheritance.title: Functional settings
settings_inheritance.introduction: Each setting either follows the consortium, or has been set for this library on its own. Change a switch to set it here; revert to follow the consortium again.
settings_inheritance.reason_revert: Reverted to inherited for {{scope}} in DCB Admin
settings_inheritance.announced_reverted: {{setting}} now follows the consortium again for this library

bulk.title: Set for chosen libraries
bulk.introduction: This writes an explicit value for each library you choose, so they keep it when the consortium changes. Reverting removes it, and those libraries follow the consortium again.
bulk.enable: Enable it for the chosen libraries
bulk.disable: Disable it for the chosen libraries
bulk.inherit: Revert them to following the consortium
bulk.too_many: Choose no more than {{max}} libraries at a time.
bulk.reason_help: Recorded against every library you change, so this can be accounted for later.
bulk.applied: Applied to {{changed}} of the {{asked}} libraries you chose.

settings_inheritance.introduction_with_group: Each setting follows the consortium, or its group, or has been set for this library on its own. Change a switch to set it here; revert to follow the wider setting again.
settings_inheritance.introduction_group: Each setting either follows the consortium, or has been set for this group. A value set here applies to every library in the group that has not set its own.
settings_inheritance.group_not_settings_bearing: Settings are carried by {{type}} groups on this deployment, so this group has none. A value set here would apply to no library.
settings_inheritance.no_group_level: No group type carries settings on this deployment, so settings resolve from a library or from the consortium.
